title: Preparation of Cleared Whole-Mount Urethra and Urinary Bladder from Mice for Immunolabeling
author: Pfeil, Dettler, et al.

steps.title: Prepare pre‑rinse solution
steps.instruction: Make a 1 L pre‑rinse solution containing 2.5 % PVP, 0.9 % NaCl and 0.5 % procaine HCl, adjust pH, store, and add heparin immediately before use.

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 25 g polyvinylpyrrolidone K30 (PVP), 9 g NaCl and 5 g procaine hydrochloride in ddH₂O to a final volume of 1000 mL in a 1.5 L Erlenmeyer flask (≈200 mL needed per animal).
Adjust the pH to 7.3–7.4 with sodium hydroxide.
Stir the solution on a magnetic stirrer for approximately 4 h (the chemicals dissolve slowly).
Store the solution for up to 4 days at 2 °C–8 °C in a suitable plastic container, or freeze at –20 °C (thaw 24 h before the experiment).
Pre‑warm the solution to mouse body temperature (≈37 °C) before perfusion.
Immediately before use, add 2 mL heparin‑sodium solution (25 000 IU per 5 mL; gives a final concentration of 10 000 IU L⁻¹).

steps.title: Prepare Zamboni fixation solution
steps.instruction: Prepare saturated picric acid, 0.1 M and 0.2 M phosphate buffers, then combine with formaldehyde to obtain 2 % PFA/15 % saturated picric acid in 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.3–7.4).

substeps.instruction: Dissolve 50 g picric acid in 1000 mL ddH₂O, let stand for 8 h to allow crystal sedimentation, then filter the supernatant twice through a pleated filter (keep the filtrate as saturated picric acid).
Prepare solution A: dissolve 31.2 g sodium dihydrogen phosphate dihydrate in 1000 mL ddH₂O.
Prepare solution B: dissolve 35.6 g disodium hydrogen phosphate dihydrate in 1000 mL ddH₂O.
Make 0.2 M phosphate buffer: mix 230 mL solution A with 770 mL ddH₂O (final volume 1 L).
Make 0.1 M phosphate buffer: mix 230 mL solution A, 770 mL solution B and 1000 mL ddH₂O (final volume 2 L).
Adjust the pH of both buffers to 7.3–7.4 with hydrochloric acid.

To prepare Zamboni solution, combine 50 mL 37 % formaldehyde (formalin), 500 mL 0.2 M phosphate buffer, and 150 mL saturated picric acid; stir on a magnetic stirrer, then add ddH₂O up to a final volume of 1 L.
Pre‑warm the Zamboni solution to mouse body temperature before perfusion.

steps.title: Perfuse organ for fixation
steps.instruction: Perfuse the mouse sequentially with pre‑rinse solution (heparin added) and then Zamboni solution, both pre‑warmed to body temperature, to remove blood and fix the tissues.

substeps.instruction: Anesthetize the mouse and secure it on a dissection platform.
Insert a 1 mL syringe with a 26 G needle into the left ventricle (or appropriate vascular access).
Perfuse with the pre‑rinse solution (≈200 mL per animal) until the effluent runs clear, indicating removal of blood.
Immediately follow with perfusion of the pre‑warmed Zamboni fixation solution (volume sufficient to fill the circulatory system, typically 10–15 mL).
Allow the fixative to circulate for the time recommended by the investigator (generally a few minutes) before proceeding to organ removal.

steps.title: Dissect bladder and urethra
steps.instruction: Harvest the urinary bladder and urethra from male or female mice, removing surrounding tissues and glands as described.

substeps.instruction: Place the mouse supine on a dissection pad under a dissecting microscope and secure it.
Remove fur and visceral fat covering the bladder and pubic bone.
Shift abdominal organs aside to expose the bladder and proximal urethra.
Male mice: cut off the penis, incise and remove the foreskin at the base of the glans (removing the preputial gland).
Female mice: locate the external urethral orifice and excise it.
Remove tissue over the pubic symphysis to expose the bone.
Incise on both sides of the pelvic bone adjacent to the symphysis, then remove the symphysis with forceps.
Male mice: excise all accessory glands (vesicular, ampullary, coagulating, dorsal and ventral prostate, vas deferens).

Male mice: cut away muscle surrounding the bulbourethral urethra; then, using forceps, grasp the penile urethra below the glans, lift, and free it from the penis with careful incisions (note the urethra is attached to the penile bone).
Female mice: lift the bladder with forceps and separate the urethra from surrounding tissue by small incisions (the urethra lies ventral to the vagina).
Collect the isolated urinary bladder and urethra for downstream clearing and immunolabeling.
